primitives.summary: A curly brace that groups a run of sibling elements (`targets`), or some `parts` of one target, with a short `label` at its tip. `enter` draws the brace on, then the label fades in.
primitives.whenToUse: Naming a group: the rows that are a model’s FEATURES, the three replicas that form a QUORUM, the slots that make one BATCH.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A status on one element (use `tag`); an area on a map (use `zone_polygon`); a link between two elements (use `connector`).

targets.description: Ids of the sibling elements the brace groups, in display order (a run next to each other).

parts.description: Optional: group only these parts (rows, slots) of a single target.

items.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Short label at the brace tip, e.g. FEATURES.

semantic.description: Brace and label colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A small card with one or two lines of text and an optional `title`, for a counterfactual or a warning: "If the lease never expires: the lock is held forever ✗". Tinted by `semantic`: problem, focus or concept. `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake (the assumption it states is ruled out).
primitives.whenToUse: A what-if, a caveat or a consequence that sits beside the diagram: the cost of the naive choice, a warning about a failure mode, an aside that explains a term. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A one-word status (use `tag`); a big statement over the whole scene (use `statement_card`); a number with a source (use `stat_card`).

to.description: Id of the element in this beat to pin to (a connector, for middle).

side.description: Side of that element: top, bottom, left, right, or middle (a connector midpoint).

pin.description: Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it.

title.description: Optional short heading above the text, e.g. WHAT IF.

text.description: The counterfactual or warning; wraps to at most two lines.

semantic.description: Colour meaning: problem (a warning), focus (the point) or concept (an aside).

primitives.summary: A single line-drawn symbol from the asset library (server, database, user, lock, cloud), in a semantic colour, with no text.
primitives.whenToUse: A visual cue next to other elements: what kind of thing is involved, or the idea of the beat (speed, security, time) at a glance.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A component the story talks about (use `node_card` with an icon); an everyday object with a caption (use `item_icon`); anything that needs a word to be understood.

asset.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

semantic.description: Stroke colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A framed detail card that zooms in over the scene while everything behind it dims. It holds other elements of the beat (`children`: e.g. a `data_block`, a `counter_transition`, a `slot_grid`, a `map_base` or a `segmented_time_bar`), drawn inside it and shown only while it is. `enter` zooms it out of its `anchor`; `exit` shrinks it back in. Children keep their own events (enter, count, highlight).
primitives.whenToUse: A closer look at one part of the diagram: what is inside a cache entry, the features a model reads for one transaction, the bins behind a warehouse pin, the time budget of one build.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Text only (use `statement_card` or `callout`); a whole new scene (start a new beat). Show at most one overlay at a time, and never put an overlay inside it.

title.description: Optional title in the panel header: what the detail shows.

anchor.description: Optional id of the element the panel zooms out of (and shrinks back into).

children.description: Ids of the elements in this beat drawn inside the panel; they show only while it does.

semantic.description: Frame colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A flat everyday object from the asset library (phone, car, ticket, parcel, pizza) on a soft tile, with a caption under it. `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake.
primitives.whenToUse: The real-world thing the system is about: the parcel, the payment card, the ticket, the user's phone. Grounds an abstract flow in something the viewer has held.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A system component (use `node_card`); a bare symbol without a caption (use `icon`); data about the object (use `data_block`).

asset.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

caption.description: What the object is in this story, shown under it.

semantic.description: Tile colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A titled card for one component of a system (a service, server, database, client or queue), with an optional subtitle and icon. `lock` adds a padlock badge; `reject` turns it red with a cross and a shake. An optional `role` badge (a crown for the leader) sits at the top centre as the part "role": `exit` it on the old holder and `enter` it on the new one to hand the role over (a role whose first part event is `enter` starts hidden).
primitives.whenToUse: The boxes of a system diagram: anything the story treats as a component that receives, holds or sends something.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A label or status (use `tag`); a quantity (use `counter`); an everyday object (use `item_icon`); a bare symbol (use `icon`).

title.description: Name of the component, shown in uppercase.

subtitle.description: Optional second line: its role or a detail. One line, at most 28 characters.

icon.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

role.description: Optional role badge (asset id, e.g. a crown for a leader) at the top centre. It is the part "role": exit it on the old holder and enter it on the new one to move the role.

semantic.description: Border and glow colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: One to three large `lines` at display size on a card that spans the stage, over the dimmed scene, each line in its own colour meaning. Long lines wrap; the text never shrinks. `enter` fades it in with a slight rise. Lines are parts: `enter` a line on its word to build the statement up, highlight or pulse the one that matters. It is an overlay: everything else on the board dims while it shows.
primitives.whenToUse: A planted question ("Why not just retry forever?"), a two-line takeaway ("Easy: copy the data. Hard: keep it in sync."), a verdict before the next chapter.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A label next to a diagram part (use `tag` or `callout`); the beat headline (that is the HUD headline); a detail view with diagram parts in it (use `inset_panel`). Show at most one overlay at a time.

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

text.description: One large line at display size; wraps rather than shrinking.

semantic.description: Colour of this line: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

lines.description: One to three lines, top to bottom, each with its own colour meaning.

primitives.summary: A boxed monospace label in a semantic colour, like a sticker on the board. It names a thing, a state or a result in two or three words ("429", "CACHE HIT", "RATE LIMITED").
primitives.whenToUse: Labelling a state, outcome or status code; calling out the key term of the beat; marking a result as ok or problem. `reject` turns it red with a cross. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Sentences or explanations (the narration and headline carry those); numbers that change (use `counter`); a component or service in a system diagram.

to.description: Id of the element in this beat to pin to (a connector, for middle).

side.description: Side of that element: top, bottom, left, right, or middle (a connector midpoint).

pin.description: Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it.

text.description: Short label, shown in uppercase monospace.

semantic.description: Colour meaning: neutral label, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A speech bubble holding one line of monospace command, with the verb coloured, such as a key/value store command or a CLI call. On `enter` the command types itself out (about 30 characters a second, never more than 1.5 s). `reject` turns it red with a cross.
primitives.whenToUse: The exact request one component sends another, when the command itself teaches something: what a client asks a cache, what a producer writes to a log.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Data at rest (use `data_block`); several lines or real code; a plain label (use `tag`).

text.description: The command exactly as typed, on one line.

semantic.description: Colour of the bubble and the command verb: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A JSON-like block of key/value pairs on a card, with an optional title. On `enter` it types in one field at a time (about a third of a second each); without `enter` all fields show at once. A field can colour its value by meaning.
primitives.whenToUse: Showing what a thing looks like as data: a booking, a cache entry, a message on a queue, the record a real object becomes. Up to 6 short fields.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Code or logic (this is data only); a single command (use `command_bubble`); long text, nested objects or lists; a single number (use `counter`).

title.description: Optional name above the block, e.g. the record type.

key.description: Field name, as it would appear in the data.

value.description: Field value: a short string, a number, true/false or null.

semantic.description: Colours the value and tints its row: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

fields.description: The key/value pairs, in display order.

primitives.summary: A card with one typeset formula (LaTeX, rendered by KaTeX) and an optional caption that reads it in plain words. At most 80 characters of LaTeX; invalid LaTeX is a spec error.
primitives.whenToUse: The one formula a topic genuinely rests on: attention scores, a hit ratio, the hash ring position. At most one per video, and only when the narration walks through it.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A single number (use `counter` or `stat_card`); an equation the narration never explains; code or data (use `data_block`).

latex.description: One formula in LaTeX math mode, without $ delimiters. Rendered by KaTeX.

caption.description: Optional plain-words reading of the formula, shown under it.

semantic.description: Border and glow colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A grid of square cells dropped over a map or zones. `enter` drops it in from above. The `cells` are parts addressed by row and column: `highlight` one to light it with its tag (e.g. HOT CELL), `pulse` it for attention, `reject` it to turn it red.
primitives.whenToUse: Turning space into buckets: geohash cells, a spatial index, a quadtree level, partitioning a city for drivers. Set `over` to the `map_base` it divides.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Irregular areas (use `zone_polygon`); a grid of items or seats (use `slot_grid`); a table of data (use `data_block`).

over.description: Optional id of the map_base or zone_polygon the grid lies over.

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

row.description: Row, counted from 1 at the top.

col.description: Column, counted from 1 at the left.

label.description: Optional tag shown when the cell lights up, e.g. HOT CELL.

semantic.description: Cell colour when lit: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

cells.description: Cells events can light up, by row and column.

primitives.summary: A stylised top-down city: blocks, streets, avenues, parks and, in the riverside `variant`, a river. A quiet background that map scenes draw on; it carries no labels. `dim` pushes it further back; `highlight` brings it forward again.
primitives.whenToUse: Any scene set in a city: ride hailing, deliveries, store coverage, nearby search. Put `route_path`, `zone_polygon` and `grid_overlay` over it.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Abstract systems with no geography (use `node_card` and `connector`); a world or region map; a background for its own sake.

variant.description: City style: downtown (dense blocks), suburb (large blocks, parks) or riverside.

primitives.summary: A dashed search circle centred on the element `around`, with an optional `label` on its rim (the radius, or what is searched). `encloses` lists elements that must sit inside it (the circle grows to fit them). `enter` grows it out from the centre.
primitives.whenToUse: A search area or reach: couriers within 2 km of a depot, servers within one network hop, the candidates a matcher considers around a target.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A named area with edges (use `zone_polygon`); a grid of cells (use `grid_overlay`); a countdown (use `timer_ring`).

around.description: Id of the element in this beat at the centre of the circle.

encloses.description: Optional ids of elements the ring must enclose (the candidates in reach); it grows to fit them.

label.description: Optional label on the ring, e.g. 2 KM.

semantic.description: Ring colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A glowing route through named `stops`, with a pin at the start and at the end and an optional `distance` tag. `enter` shows the pins; `move` draws the route from the first stop to the last (the tag lands when it arrives), with the optional `mover` riding its head. `mode` smooth draws a curve instead of street legs. `mode` jumpy shows raw position pings: each `move` hops the `mover` to the next stop (one `move` per stop after the first), then a `morph` draws a smooth curve through the stops and the mover glides along it. Stops are parts: highlight one, or reject it (a red cross: closed, unreachable).
primitives.whenToUse: A journey on a map: a driver to a pickup, a parcel from store to door, a packet hopping between regions. Put it over a `map_base`. Jumpy then smooth: raw GPS pings vs an interpolated track.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A link between two components (use `connector`); traffic over time (use `packet_stream`); areas on a map (use `zone_polygon`).

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Short name of the place, e.g. a pickup point.

stops.description: Named stops in travel order, first to last.

distance.description: Optional distance or time tag shown at the end, e.g. 4.2 km.

mode.description: Optional: jumpy (the mover hops stop to stop, one per move, until a morph smooths the route) or smooth (move draws a curve through the stops). Omit for street-like legs.

mover.description: Optional asset id of what travels the route (a bike, a car, a parcel).

semantic.description: Route colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: Labelled areas drawn as soft, irregular shapes that can overlap. The `zones` are parts: `highlight` one to make it glow, `reject` to turn it red (overloaded, out of service), `dim` to push it back, `enter` to reveal it on its own word.
primitives.whenToUse: Regions on a map or coverage areas: delivery zones, cell towers, shards by region, availability zones. Put it over a `map_base`.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A regular grid of cells (use `grid_overlay`); components with names (use `node_card`); items in slots (use `slot_grid`).

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Name of the area, e.g. a delivery zone.

semantic.description: Zone colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

overlap.description: Whether neighbouring zones overlap (shared coverage) or keep a gap.

primitives.summary: An arrow or line from one element to another, with an optional label at its middle. `enter` draws it from `from` to `to`; each `move` sends one glowing packet along it; `reject` turns it red with a cross at the middle (the link is broken or refused).
primitives.whenToUse: A relation or a hop between two elements already in the beat: a request from client to server, a write to a database, a replica link. Use `move` on the word where one thing travels.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Continuous traffic (add a `packet_stream` along the connector); a journey on a map (use `route_path`); a queue of waiting items (use `conveyor_queue`).

from.description: Id of the element in this beat where the connector starts.

to.description: Id of the element in this beat it points to.

label.description: Optional label at the middle: what travels, or the relation.

heads.description: Arrowheads: end (one-way arrow), both (two-way) or none (plain line).

dashed.description: Dashed: an optional, async or planned link.

semantic.description: Line colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A horizontal belt carrying labelled blocks toward its right end, where they are taken. `items` are parts, listed in arrival order: `enter` slides one in from the left behind the others, `exit` takes it off the belt (it lifts away and the rest move up), `lock` marks it as claimed, `reject` turns it red. An item is on the belt from the start unless it first appears with `enter`.
primitives.whenToUse: Work waiting its turn: orders in a queue, jobs for a worker, messages in a partition. Take items on the words where they are processed.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Traffic that never waits (use `packet_stream`); items on a shelf or seats picked in any order (use `slot_grid`); a count of waiting work (use `counter`).

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Short label on the block, e.g. an order number.

semantic.description: Block colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

items.description: Blocks in arrival order: the first is at the front and is taken first.

label.description: Optional caption under the belt: what the queue is.

primitives.summary: A steady stream of small packets flowing along a `connector`, at `rate` packets per second. `enter` starts the flow from the source; `exit` stops sending (packets in flight still arrive); `reject` blocks the stream before the target: packets turn red and vanish at a barrier.
primitives.whenToUse: Ongoing traffic between two elements: requests pouring into a server, events into a queue, replication. Raise `rate` to show load growing.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A single request or hop (a move on the `connector` itself); items waiting in order (use `conveyor_queue`); a number of requests (use `counter`).

along.description: Id of the connector in this beat that the packets travel along.

semantic.description: Packet colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A big number with an optional unit and caption. Without a `count` event it shows `value`. With one, it shows `from` (default 0) until the count begins, then counts up or down to `value`, so the viewer watches a quantity grow or drain. With `ticking` the count runs on narration time and lands on `value` exactly at the `reject` (an outage clock that stops when the outage ends). `reject` turns the number red with a shake.
primitives.whenToUse: One quantity that matters to the story: requests per second, tokens left, queue length, latency, how long an outage lasted. Use `count` when the change itself is the point. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A word or status instead of a quantity (use `tag`); a countdown in time; several numbers at once (one counter per number, and only the ones the story needs).

to.description: Id of the element in this beat to pin to (a connector, for middle).

side.description: Side of that element: top, bottom, left, right, or middle (a connector midpoint).

pin.description: Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it.

value.description: The number shown once any count has finished.

from.description: Where a `count` starts (default 0). Shown until the count begins.

label.description: Caption under the number.

semantic.description: Colour of the number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

ticking.description: Count on narration time: the count runs from its word until the `reject` (else the exit or the end of the beat), like a clock. Without it a count takes under a second.

primitives.summary: A big number changing to another, shown as "10 → 9": the old number in one colour, an arrow, the new number in another. Without a `count` event it shows the change as done. With one, the old number stands alone until the count, then the arrow and the new number come in and the old one fades back. A null `from` shows "?": an unknown value revealed as a prediction or a measured result ("? → 0.82").
primitives.whenToUse: One discrete change the story turns on: 10 free lockers dropping to 9, a version going from 1 to 2, a retry count ticking up. The colour change carries the meaning (e.g. neutral to problem). With `from` null: a prediction appearing, an unknown measured for the first time.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A quantity that counts smoothly up or down (use `counter`); a countdown in time; more than one change at once.

from.description: The number before the change, or null when it is unknown (shown as "?").

unit.description: Short unit after the new number.

label.description: Caption under the numbers.

fromSemantic.description: Colour of the old number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

toSemantic.description: Colour of the new number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A stacked bar splitting a time budget into steps (BUILD | TEST), each segment as wide as its time with its mm:ss under it, and the total at the top right. With `budgetSec`, a marker shows the budget and any time past it turns red. `enter` fills the segments left to right; segments are parts: highlight the step being discussed, reject the one that blows the budget.
primitives.whenToUse: Where time goes in a flow: a 10-minute delivery promise, the latency budget of a request, the stages of a deploy. Use it when the split matters more than one number.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A single countdown (use `timer_ring`); one number (use `counter` or `stat_card`); steps without durations (use `node_card` and `connector`).

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Short name of the step, e.g. BUILD or TEST.

sec.description: How long the step takes, in seconds.

semantic.description: Segment colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

segments.description: Steps in order, left to right (1 to 5).

budgetSec.description: Optional time budget: a marker on the bar; time past it is drawn red.

label.description: Optional caption: what the time is for, e.g. COMMIT TO DEPLOY.

primitives.summary: A card with one big figure, a label under it, and a small source footnote. The figure is text, so units and formatting stay as written ("10k/s", "₹2,000 Cr", "99.9%").
primitives.whenToUse: A cited real-world number that makes the problem concrete: traffic at peak, money lost, a benchmark. Every figure from research needs its source.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A number that animates or changes (use `counter` or `counter_transition`); an illustrative number with no source (use `counter`); a label or status (use `tag`).

value.description: The figure as displayed, units included.

label.description: What the figure measures.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, shown as a footnote. Required.

semantic.description: Colour of the value: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A countdown ring with the time left as mm:ss in the middle. It shows `durationSec` until `count` starts the clock. Its pace is set by the narration: it reaches 00:00 exactly on the `reject` (expiry: empty ring, red flash); without `reject` it runs out at the element's `exit` or the end of the beat, and holds 00:00. It never runs slower than real time; when faster, a fast-forward tag shows the multiplier (e.g. 60×).
primitives.whenToUse: A deadline or hold in the story: a room held for 10 minutes, a token that expires, a lease or a timeout. Put `count` where the clock starts and `reject` on the word where the time runs out. Set `pin` to keep it on a side of the element it belongs to.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A quantity that is not time (use `counter`); elapsed time across the whole video (that is the story clock in the HUD); a duration that never runs down.

to.description: Id of the element in this beat to pin to (a connector, for middle).

side.description: Side of that element: top, bottom, left, right, or middle (a connector midpoint).

pin.description: Optional: pin this element to another one so it stays attached to it.

durationSec.description: Time on the clock when it starts, in seconds (600 shows 10:00).

label.description: Caption under the ring: what the time is for.

semantic.description: Ring colour while running: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A generic phone or tablet outline (`kind`) with a simple screen: a `status` line, list `rows`, and a `button`. `morph` changes the button to its "then" label and colour (Claim → Claimed ✓). Rows are parts: enter one as it arrives, highlight it, or reject it (red with a cross: declined, failed). Never a real app, screenshot or logo.
primitives.whenToUse: What a user sees: an incoming task, a request to approve, a list of notifications, the status of a payment.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A server or service (use `node_card`); a phone as an everyday object without a screen (use `item_icon`); data fields (use `data_block`).

status.description: Optional status line at the top of the screen.

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Row text: a task, a contact, a message.

detail.description: Optional short value at the right, e.g. 3 MIN.

icon.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

rows.description: Optional list rows, top to bottom.

label.description: Button text, e.g. Claim.

semantic.description: Button colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

then.description: Optional label and colour the button changes to on morph.

label.description: Button text, e.g. Claimed ✓.

semantic.description: Button colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A grid of labelled slots: bins of stock, a shelf, cinema seats or documents. Each slot is a part: `lock` claims it (padlock, yellow), `highlight` picks it out, `exit` takes its item (it lifts away and leaves an empty outline), `enter` puts an item back, `reject` turns it red with a cross (sold out, conflict).
primitives.whenToUse: Contention over specific items: two users grabbing the same locker, stock picked from bins, which documents a search touches. Address the slots on the words that act on them.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Items moving in order (use `conveyor_queue`); a spatial grid over a map (use `grid_overlay`); one standalone object (use `item_icon`).

kind.description: How slots look: inventory (bins), shelf (rows on planks), seats, documents.

id.description: Part id, unique in this element; events act on it with params.parts.

label.description: Short label on the slot, e.g. a slot number or an item name.

icon.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

semantic.description: Slot colour: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.

slots.description: The slots, in reading order (1 to 24).

cols.description: Slots per row; omit to choose from the slot count.

label.description: Optional caption under the grid.

patterns.summary: Two halves side by side get the same event at the same moment, and each shows its own outcome: the side that handles it lights up with its verdict, the side that fails turns red.
patterns.whenToUse: Comparing two designs under one condition: SQL vs NoSQL under a write burst, sync vs async on a slow call, temperature 0 vs 1 on one prompt.
patterns.whenNotToUse: A near and a far store (use `cache_hit_miss`); a slow way then a fast way in sequence (use `brute_force_then_index`).

anchors.name: show
anchors.description: Both sides appear.

anchors.name: event
anchors.description: The same event reaches both sides at once.

anchors.name: verdict
anchors.description: Each side shows how it handled it.

targets.description: The shared event tag.
The left side.
The right side.
Arrow from the event to the left side.
Arrow from the event to the right side.
The verdict tag on the left.
The verdict tag on the right.

event.description: The one event both sides get, as a short tag, e.g. 10K WRITES.

title.description: Name of this side (a design, a system, a setting).

icon.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

verdict.description: What happens on this side, as a short tag, e.g. 2 MS or DATA LOST.

outcome.description: ok (handles it: the side lights up) or problem (fails: the side turns red).

title.description: Name of this side (a design, a system, a setting).

icon.description: Asset id from the asset library (an unknown id is drawn as a placeholder and reported).

verdict.description: What happens on this side, as a short tag, e.g. 2 MS or DATA LOST.

outcome.description: ok (handles it: the side lights up) or problem (fails: the side turns red).

event.description: The same event reaches both sides at once.

verdict.description: Each side shows how it handled it.

at.description: Narration anchors: the word (or beat edge) for each moment.

patterns.summary: A brute-force search checks every item and each turns red, with a tag naming the cost. Then an index appears and jumps straight to the one item, which lights up.
patterns.whenToUse: Brute force before the clever fix: a full table scan vs an index, checking every zone vs a grid cell lookup, a linear search vs a hash map.
patterns.whenNotToUse: A fast and a slow store side by side (use `cache_hit_miss`); two whole designs compared (use `versus_split`).

anchors.name: scan
anchors.description: Every item is checked one by one and turns red.

patterns.summary: Two requests race for one resource. The first arrives and locks it (padlock) and a hold timer starts; the second arrives while it is held, its arrow turns red and it is tagged with a cross. With a `release` anchor, the hold timer runs out there and the resource is released.
patterns.whenToUse: Contention for one thing: two users booking the same room, two workers claiming the same job, two writers on one row. The moment the lock makes the second attempt fail.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Rejecting a repeat of the same request (use `reject_duplicate`); many requests overwhelming a server (use `flood_then_funnel`).

patterns.summary: A client with a near store and a far store. A hit is answered by the near store and tagged with its small latency; a miss goes on to the far store and is tagged with its large one, so the gap in latency is the lesson.
patterns.whenToUse: Caching, CDNs and any near/far trade-off: cache vs database, edge vs origin, memory vs disk, KV cache vs recomputation.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Comparing two whole designs side by side (use `versus_split`); a flood of requests on one node (use `flood_then_funnel`).

patterns.whenToUse: Idempotency and deduplication: a payment retried after a timeout, a message delivered twice, a double-clicked submit.
patterns.whenNotToUse: Two different requests competing for one resource (use `atomic_lock`); a request that fails for another reason (use a `tag` or `callout`).

patterns.summary: Two regions with a leader and a replica. The link breaks (red, then dashed) and an outage clock counts up; cut off, the replica takes the role badge too. patterns.whenToUse: Network partitions and split brain: two primaries after a partition, fencing and leases, why quorums exist; the real-incident beat after a `failover` concept beat.
patterns.whenNotToUse: A clean failover where the old leader is really gone (use `failover`); a single request refused under a lock (use `atomic_lock`).
